collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The great stone wall was built by workers left out of its story: add their names, or tell the whole truth too.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has found that the great stone wall, said to be built by the village's first leader, was really built by many workers whose names were left out of every song. Some of their descendants still live in the village. (friend) says the old songs should not be changed. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The workers' names are found, as many as can be, and carved on the wall. Their descendants come to touch them. The old song gets a new verse. (friend) sings it, gruffly.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) tells the whole story at the gathering: the workers, and the leader who took the credit. Some villagers are upset to have their hero lessened. Others say it was long overdue. The names are carved, and the argument goes on.
